findings: The nonblocking root-owned global lock rejects concurrent owners and does not replace an existing lock inode.

The sealed parent binds job, source, uid/gid, cwd, boot, exact parent inode/limits/unit bytes and systemd properties; reuse is restricted to the current-ELF registry and requires no remaining children.
The fixed systemd parent retains CPU 25000/100000, memory 2147483648, swap 0, pids 256; service uses original uid/gid, NoNewPrivileges, empty capability bounding set and control-group cleanup.
The exact direct libtest parent executable and cwd are observed; both libtest and launcher process identities are verified around pidfd_open and monitored while the native child runs.
The original selector argv, source and binary before/after, native log and architecture 18-sample report are bound. Late cleanup or parent seal failure invalidates success.
limits: This review executed no native fixture, systemd setup, Cargo, cgroup or Host qualification.
Only architecture receives the explicit 120-second adapter timeout. Other fixtures retain their original native budgets and CI supervisor lifetime.
The root-owned seal is not an authorization barrier against malicious root/passwordless-sudo same-job code; the event-bound reviewed source remains the trust boundary.
No business, performance, public admission or all-honest gate is closed by this review.
Rust child-marker and actual KernelBudget verification were independently reviewed by the Chain owner, not re-executed here.
